newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF shares rise on outlook in H1 report.
newsitem.headline: SKF shares rise on outlook in H1 report.

text.p: Shares in bearings maker SKF rose on Tuesday after the company's half year report showed an improving trend even though profits were lower than in first half 1996.
SKF shares rose eight crowns to 220 in early trade but by 0900 GMT settled back to 215 crowns.
Brokers said the market reacted positively to the fact that SKF's markets were stronger in the second quarter of 1997 than in the first.
"Sales volumes increased by four percent in the first half which means volumes rose eight percent in the second quarter," said Swedbank analyst Mats Larsson.
The company said these improving trends were continuing.

But brokers said the share rose more than expected, particularly as the company did not announce any restructuring as speculated in the wake of a positive reaction to appliance maker Electrolux's radical shakeup announced in June.

SKF posted a profit after financial items of 1.10 billion crowns for the six months ending June 30 compared to 1.48 billion a year ago. The market expected 1.13 billion crowns, according to a Reuters poll.
